---
title: "🚀 Get started"
description: >
  Install faofishingreport, update the FAO data, produce the first charts for the
  Northeast Atlantic (FAO area 27) and write a Word report in one call.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
```

```{r data-source, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
data_source()
```

**faofishingreport** turns the FAO Global Capture Production statistics into charts, maps
and tables for reports. This page walks through a complete first analysis of the
**Northeast Atlantic (FAO major fishing area 27)**; every chart below was produced by
the code shown above it.

A typical workflow:

| Step | What you do | Functions |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Data | Check for and download the latest FAO release; see which release you use | `check_fao_update()`, `download_fao_data()`, `fao_data_info()` |
| 2. Fishing area | Total catch, main species and main countries of an area | `fishing_area_data()`, `fishing_area_species()`, `fishing_area_country()` |
| 3. Species and countries | Who catches a species, what a country catches | `species_country()`, `country_species()`, `country_analysis()` |
| 4. Summaries | Composition, stock status, trends, data quality, diversity, fleets | `species_group_composition()`, `stock_status()`, `peak_trend()`, `data_quality()`, `coastal_distant()`, ... |
| 5. Methods from the literature | Catch shocks, collapses, synchrony, pelagic/demersal ratio, mean temperature of the catch | `catch_shocks()`, `collapse_analysis()`, `catch_synchrony()`, `pelagic_demersal()`, `mean_temperature_catch()` |
| 6. Stock assessment | CMSY++ for the main species | `cmsy_setup()`, `cmsy_area()` |
| 7. Report | A Word report of an area in one call | `fao_report()` |
| 8. Style | Language, theme, colours, map projection | `fao_settings()` |

## 📦 Installation

faofishingreport needs **R 4.2 or later**. Install it from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Linbojun99/faofishingreport", dependencies = TRUE)
```

With `dependencies = TRUE` every package that the analyses use is installed with it: dplyr,
ggplot2 and sf for the charts and maps, rnaturalearth for the world maps, officer and xml2 for
Word reports, eoffice for editable PowerPoint charts, nanoparquet for the FishBase and
SeaLifeBase tables, ncdf4 for sea surface temperature files, and the R packages of CMSY++
(coda, conicfit, gplots, MASS, mvtnorm, neuralnet, ...). The only exceptions are rjags and
R2jags, which need the separate JAGS program: `cmsy_setup()` installs JAGS and both packages
the first time you use CMSY++ (see [📉 CMSY++ stock assessment](cmsy.html)).

::: callout-note
**Windows and macOS** use binary packages, so no compiler (Rtools) is needed. On macOS,
editable PowerPoint charts also need [XQuartz](https://www.xquartz.org).
**Linux** needs the system libraries of the sf package and, for Chinese charts, a Chinese font:

```bash
sudo apt-get install libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libudunits2-dev fonts-noto-cjk
```
:::

Load the package. The start-up message shows the operating system and the font chosen for
charts (SimSun on Windows, Songti SC on macOS, Noto Serif CJK SC on Linux):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(faofishingreport)
#> faofishingreport: Windows, chart font "SimSun" (change it with fao_font())
```

## 💾 Get the latest FAO data

The package comes with FAO release `r fao_data_info("bundled")$release`.
FAO publishes a new release about once a year. Check whether a newer one exists and download
it (about 5 MB, a few seconds):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
check_fao_update()
#> FAO Global Capture Production
#>   Latest online release: 2026.1.0 (published 2026-03-30)
#>   Bundled with package:  2026.1.0
#>   Downloaded locally:    none
#>   Your data is up to date.

download_fao_data()   # only needed when a newer release is available
```

All functions automatically use the newest data available. `fao_data_info()` tells which
release that is, where it comes from and how to cite it. See [💾 FAO data](data.html) for all
the arguments of these functions, choosing releases, the data format and working with your
own subsets.

## 📁 Where the results go

Each analysis saves its charts and tables in the **current working folder**:

| Folder | Content |
|---|---|
| `figures/png/` | Charts as PNG (always); the summary analyses use `figures/png/summary/` |
| `figures/pptx/` | Charts as editable PowerPoint files (with `pptx = TRUE`; uses the eoffice package) |
| `tables/` | Tables as CSV, readable by Excel including Chinese names |
| `reports/` | Word reports of `fao_report()` |

So start by choosing a folder for the report:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
setwd("D:/reports/FAO27")   # any folder
```

## 🌊 First analysis: FAO area 27

`fishing_area_data()` extracts the catch of one FAO major fishing area and draws its total catch
with the breakpoints of the mean catch, its share of the world catch of all marine areas, and a
world map of the countries fishing there.

```{r, figures = TRUE}
FAO27 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

The result is a list with the catch records of the area (`area_data`), the periods between
breakpoints (`coefs_data`) and the map data (`act_world_map`). `FAO27$area_data` is the input of
most other functions:

```{r}
show_table(FAO27$area_data, n = 5)
```

Any other area works the same way. The names of the FAO major fishing areas are:

```{r}
data <- load_fao_data()
sort(unique(data$FAO.major.fishing.area..Name.))
```

## 🐟 Main species and countries

The ten species with the largest catch in area 27, their catch over time and the breakpoints of
their mean catch:

```{r, figures = TRUE}
species <- fishing_area_species(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 10))
```

The same for the countries:

```{r, figures = TRUE}
countries <- fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 10))
```

## 🌐 Chinese and bilingual charts

Every analysis has a `lang` argument: `"en"` (English), `"zh"` (Chinese) or `"both"`.
Country, species and area names use the official FAO Chinese names.

```{r, figures = "country_ranked_wrap"}
species_country(FAO27$area_data, species_name = "Atlantic cod", lang = "both")
```

To use Chinese everywhere, set it once with `fao_settings(lang = "zh")`.

## 📊 A first summary: stock status

`stock_status()` classifies each species by its catch relative to its peak catch (stock status
plots, Kleisner et al. 2013):

```{r, figures = TRUE}
status <- stock_status(FAO27$area_data)
```

## 📝 A Word report in one call

`fao_report()` runs the analyses of an area and writes a Word report with cover, abstract,
data sources and methods, results with charts and tables, conclusions, references and appendix
tables. The area can be given by its name or its code:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_report(27, lang = "en")   # writes reports/FAO27_report_en.docx in the working folder
```

By default the report has the total catch and its stages, the main species and countries, the
ISSCAAP groups, the stock status plots, the data quality, the diversity of the catch and the
coastal and distant-water fleets. Catch shocks, collapses, synchrony, the pelagic/demersal ratio,
the mean temperature of the catch, distant-water fleet profiles and CMSY++ can be switched on.
See [📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF](report.html) for all its settings.

## ⚙️ Settings of the functions on this page

The arguments shared by the analyses:

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: the language of `fao_settings()` (`"en"` unless changed) |
| `plot` | Save the charts | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the tables in `tables/` (not in `fishing_area_data()`) | `TRUE` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `ZH = TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` (only in the fishing area, species and country functions) | `FALSE` |
| `label` | Name used in the output files of the summary analyses, e.g. `stock_status()` | `NULL`: the fishing area (or country) of the data |

Every function has its own arguments as well; each article has a table of all of them:

| Functions | Main arguments | All arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `check_fao_update()`, `download_fao_data()`, `load_fao_data()`, `fao_data_info()` | `version`, `data_dir`, `overwrite`, `quiet` | [💾 FAO data](data.html) |
| `fishing_area_data()` | `area_name`, `timeseries_analysis`, `data_version`, colours and text sizes | [🌊 Fishing area analysis](fishing-areas.html) |
| `fishing_area_species()`, `fishing_area_country()` | `rank_range`, `timeseries_analysis`, `h_value`, line and text styles | [🌊 Fishing area analysis](fishing-areas.html) |
| `species_country()` | `species_name`, `rank_range`, `h_value`, map style | [🐟 Species and countries](species-countries.html) |
| `stock_status()` | `taxon_levels`, `min_years`, `min_consecutive`, `min_catch`, `smooth` | [📈 Composition, stock status and trends](status-trends.html) |
| `fao_report()` | `area`, `lang`, `file`, sections switched on or off, settings of each analysis | [📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF](report.html) |
| `fao_settings()`, `fao_font()` | `lang`, `theme`, `palette`, `map_projection`, `dpi`, ... | [🎨 Customise charts and maps](customise.html) |
